paper_id: Wang et al. - 2013 - BlindDate A Neighbor Discovery Protocol
title: BlindDate: A Neighbor Discovery Protocol
motivation: Mobile apps (gaming/coupons) need devices to discover each other locally without server; urban sensor networks need efficient handheld-to-node discovery under 4% duty cycle
problem_framing: Asynchronous neighbor discovery: symmetric case (same duty cycle, async clocks) and asymmetric case (different duty cycles). Goal: guarantee active slot overlap between devices with low latency
key_insight: Multiple Dynamic slots with opposite moving directions (vs Searchlight's single moving probe) increases overlap probability; bouncing strategy (step=2) halves hyper-period
method_signature: Deterministic BD protocol with Static+Dynamic slots, k=2 dynamic blocks out of m=5 total blocks, using bouncing (step=2) movement
evaluation_criteria: Worst-case discovery latency bound and average latency, under same duty cycle for fair comparison across protocols
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Theoretical asymmetric bound is loose (we believe real performance is much better); cannot find feasible solution for p=1 (optimal even case) and settle for p=2
evidence_for_taste: we observe that there is little chance for overlap
we consider adding more probe slots
the bouncing Dynamic slots of opposite directions often jump over each other
we propose an approach to overcome this issue
we only give a loose worst-case bound
thinking_moves: 观察到单 probe slot 同向移动时 overlap 概率低, 从而想到用多 probe slot 反向移动
先分析 k 和 m 的 case-by-case 关系, 确定最优参数组合 (k=2, m=5)
发现 bouncing 策略导致 slots 跳过的副作用后, 通过延长邻近 slot 长度来补偿
把 worst-case latency 表示成 duty cycle 的函数, 在相同参数下形式化比较
